scenes.heading: Understanding a purchase contract and contingencies

sents.d: Understanding a purchase contract and contingencies
Contingencies protect a buyer, but too many can make an offer less competitive.

Common contingencies — inspection, financing, appraisal — give a buyer a way to exit the contract if something goes wrong, but each one added also makes an offer less attractive to a seller in a competitive market, so balancing protection against competitiveness is a real skill.

Explaining these tradeoffs clearly to clients (rather than assuming they understand contract mechanics) is part of the value an agent provides, and prevents a client from either taking on too much risk or losing a house over an unnecessary contingency.
Deadlines within the contract (inspection period, financing commitment date) need active tracking — missing one can mean losing an earnest money deposit or an otherwise-avoidable contract dispute.

take: Balance contingencies with competitiveness and track deadlines.
